note: From an OpenStreetMap export (tools/osm-to-kit.mjs, 8 October 2026): the platform length (the export maps one platform area; the second is set to match) and the footbridge at the north end. Two side platforms 1.68 m outside the slow lines by the depot, the tracks at their real spacing. The real Ardwick is one island platform on the Hope Valley lines beside the main line (geograph 4247094); here it serves the stopper, so it has a platform each side, a game choice. Positive v is east. Photos (geograph 6113205 Gerald England 2019, 1374380 David Long 2009, 4247094 and 4247105 Nigel Thompson 2014; Commons 'Ardwick railway station footbridge (1)' and '(2)', Rept0n1x 2015): the footbridge is riveted plate girders under a diamond-lattice parapet, rust brown, open to the sky, on lattice trestles with brick bases, and its stairs come down in straight open flights along the line with a landing on a trestle between (the `lattice` and `flights` parts). Its deck height is from the step counts and clears the wires; how many tracks its main span crosses the photos can't settle, so it spans the line. A small blue shelter on the platform, white lamp columns with blue bases, no car park, cycle stands or ticket office. The brick booking hut is the game's: the photos show none (Commons 'Ardwick railway station (2)' and '(4)', 2015). Trains stop 8 m north of the station's point, in the middle of the platforms; the extension runs 20 m south as well as 40 m north, so a six-car unit stands wholly alongside (a game choice, the real platform takes fewer). The ticket barriers, the kiosk and the vending machine stand south of the stair foot, the lifts beside the bridge's north side (the real station has neither). A departure board on each platform. The Marple line (13 October 2026) runs past the platforms' east side, as the real Hope Valley lines do: the depot's shed stands beyond it in the Siemens depot's yard (OpenStreetMap's outline, the main API), a steel shed from memory, and the fence stops short of where the line crosses it. Across the line at real scale since 13 October 2026 (it was 1.25 times).
